requirements.title: Completeness and accuracy
requirements.text: Every current source record reaches each layer and the warehouse complete and unchanged, row by row and in aggregate.

requirements.title: Deduplication and deletes
requirements.text: Redelivered change events are kept once, the latest change per key wins, and records deleted in the source are removed from current state.

requirements.title: Full history
requirements.text: Every change is kept exactly once with a clean validity timeline per key, including deletes as tombstones.

requirements.title: Dimensional model integrity
requirements.text: Keys are unique, every fact finds its dimension rows, and type 2 dimensions are joined at the point in time of the event.

requirements.title: Partitioning
requirements.text: Facts and raw events sit in complete monthly partitions, nothing falls outside the plan, and date filters read only the partitions they need.

requirements.title: Controlled schema changes
requirements.text: Every layer matches a versioned, reviewed contract; breaking changes fail, compatible changes are reported.

requirements.title: Incremental loads
requirements.text: Loading data incrementally gives the same result as a full rebuild, whatever the arrival order, and re-running a load changes nothing.

requirements.title: Proven detection
requirements.text: Every check is shown to detect the defect it is designed for.

requirements.title: Production monitoring
requirements.text: The live warehouse is checked on a schedule for quality, freshness, volume and drift; results are stored and failures alerted.

requirements.title: Personal data protection
requirements.text: No unapproved personal data is stored, and approved personal data is visible only to authorised roles.

requirements.title: Grounded GenAI output
requirements.text: Generated safety narratives count exactly, invent nothing, disclose serious events, and the service keeps working when the model does not.

requirements.title: Reproducible test data
requirements.text: Test data is synthetic, seeded and documented with exact figures.

requirements.title: Traceable, retained evidence
requirements.text: Every requirement is traced to the tests that verify it, and each run's evidence is retained with tamper-evident hashes.

data_quality.name: sql/checks/rules/history/scd2_no_overlap.sql on dwh.dim_site
data_quality.description: The versions of one site_id in dim_site form a clean timeline.
data_quality.sql: -- Rule: the versions of one site_id in dim_site form a clean timeline. -- Each version must end exactly where the next one starts: no overlap and no gap. A version may be -- empty (valid_from = valid_to) when two changes carry the same timestamp; it never ends before it -- starts. Ties are ordered by valid_to, so an empty version sorts before the one that replaced it. SELECT site_id, valid_from, valid_to, next_valid_from FROM ( SELECT site_id, valid_from, valid_to, LEAD(valid_from) OVER (PARTITION BY site_id ORDER BY valid_from, valid_to) AS next_valid_from FROM dwh.dim_site ) versions WHERE valid_from > valid_to OR (next_valid_from IS NOT NULL AND valid_to <> next_valid_from)

data_quality.name: sql/checks/rules/history/scd2_point_in_time_site.sql on dwh
data_quality.description: Each adverse event points at the site version that was valid at 00:00 UTC on its
data_quality.sql: -- Rule: each adverse event points at the site version that was valid at 00:00 UTC on its -- onset date, not simply at the current version of the site. SELECT f.ae_id, f.onset_date, f.site_sk AS loaded_site_sk, expected.site_sk AS expected_site_sk FROM dwh.fact_adverse_event f JOIN dwh.dim_subject ds ON ds.subject_sk = f.subject_sk LEFT JOIN dwh.dim_site expected ON expected.site_id = ds.site_id AND f.onset_date::timestamptz >= expected.valid_from AND f.onset_date::timestamptz < expected.valid_to WHERE expected.site_sk IS DISTINCT FROM f.site_sk

data_quality.name: sql/checks/rules/history/scd2_single_current.sql on dwh.dim_site
data_quality.description: Exactly one current version per site_id in dim_site, and it is the open-ended one.
data_quality.sql: -- Rule: exactly one current version per site_id in dim_site, and it is the open-ended one. SELECT site_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_current) AS current_versions, max(valid_to) AS last_valid_to FROM dwh.dim_site GROUP BY site_id HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_current) <> 1 OR bool_or(is_current AND valid_to <> timestamptz '9999-12-31 00:00:00+00')

data_quality.name: sql/checks/rules/partitions/partition_plan.sql on dwh.fact_adverse_event
data_quality.description: Fact_adverse_event has one partition per month from 2025-01-01 to 2026-12-01, each exactly one
data_quality.sql: -- Rule: fact_adverse_event has one partition per month from 2025-01-01 to 2026-12-01, each exactly one -- calendar month wide, named <table>_YYYYMM after its lower bound, plus a DEFAULT partition. -- Returns one row per problem found in the catalog. WITH parts AS ( SELECT c.relname AS partition_name, pg_get_expr(c.relpartbound, c.oid) AS bound FROM pg_inherits i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.inhrelid JOIN pg_class p ON p.oid = i.inhparent JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'dwh' AND p.relname = 'fact_adverse_event' ), ranges AS ( SELECT partition_name, substring(bound FROM 'FROM \(''([^'']+)''\)')::date AS lower_bound, substring(bound FROM 'TO \(''([^'']+)''\)')::date AS upper_bound FROM parts WHERE bound <> 'DEFAULT' ), expected AS ( SELECT m::date AS month FROM generate_series(date '2025-01-01', date '2026-12-01', interval '1 month') AS m ) SELECT e.month AS month, NULL::text AS partition_name, 'missing partition' AS problem FROM expected e LEFT JOIN ranges r ON r.lower_bound = e.month WHERE r.partition_name IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT r.lower_bound, r.partition_name, 'not exactly one calendar month' FROM ranges r WHERE extract(DAY FROM r.lower_bound) <> 1 OR r.upper_bound <> (r.lower_bound + interval '1 month')::date UNION ALL SELECT r.lower_bound, r.partition_name, 'name does not match its bounds' FROM ranges r WHERE r.partition_name <> 'fact_adverse_event_' || to_char(r.lower_bound, 'YYYYMM') UNION ALL SELECT NULL, NULL, 'no DEFAULT partition' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parts WHERE bound = 'DEFAULT')

WITH parts AS ( SELECT c.relname AS partition_name, pg_get_expr(c.relpartbound, c.oid) AS bound FROM pg_inherits i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.inhrelid JOIN pg_class p ON p.oid = i.inhparent JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'dwh' AND p.relname = 'fact_visit' ), ranges AS ( SELECT partition_name, substring(bound FROM 'FROM \(''([^'']+)''\)')::date AS lower_bound, substring(bound FROM 'TO \(''([^'']+)''\)')::date AS upper_bound FROM parts WHERE bound <> 'DEFAULT' ), expected AS ( SELECT m::date AS month FROM generate_series(date '2025-01-01', date '2026-12-01', interval '1 month') AS m ) SELECT e.month AS month, NULL::text AS partition_name, 'missing partition' AS problem FROM expected e LEFT JOIN ranges r ON r.lower_bound = e.month WHERE r.partition_name IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT r.lower_bound, r.partition_name, 'not exactly one calendar month' FROM ranges r WHERE extract(DAY FROM r.lower_bound) <> 1 OR r.upper_bound <> (r.lower_bound + interval '1 month')::date UNION ALL SELECT r.lower_bound, r.partition_name, 'name does not match its bounds' FROM ranges r WHERE r.partition_name <> 'fact_visit_' || to_char(r.lower_bound, 'YYYYMM') UNION ALL SELECT NULL, NULL, 'no DEFAULT partition' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parts WHERE bound = 'DEFAULT')

data_quality.description: No column in {schema} has a name that suggests personal data (birth, email, phone, address, national id, name...) unless it is on the approved list ('dim_site.investigator', 'v_site_current.investigator', 'v_adverse_event_detail.investigator_at_onset').

data_quality.name: sql/checks/rules/privacy/personal_data_values.sql on dwh
data_quality.description: No text value anywhere in {schema} looks like an e-mail address, a phone number or a Romanian national ID (CNP). Scans every text column of every table and view.
data_quality.sql: -- Rule: no text value anywhere in dwh looks like an e-mail address, a phone number or a Romanian national ID (CNP). Scans every text column of every table and view. SELECT table_name, column_name, matches FROM ( SELECT c.table_name, c.column_name, (xpath('/row/n/text()', query_to_xml(format( 'SELECT count(*) AS n FROM %I.%I WHERE %I ~ %L', c.table_schema, c.table_name, c.column_name, '([A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}|\+?[0-9][0-9 ()-]{8,}[0-9]|\m[1-8][0-9]{12}\M)' ), false, true, '')))[1]::text::int AS matches FROM information_schema.columns c WHERE c.table_schema = 'dwh' AND c.data_type IN ('text', 'character varying', 'character') ) scanned WHERE matches > 0

mutations.story: Facts were joined to the current site version instead of the version valid at onset
The monthly safety view joined the SCD2 site dimension on site_id instead of site_sk, fanning out rows
The is_current flag was not reset when a newer site version arrived
A migration changed a numeric column to text, which breaks sorting and aggregation downstream
A boolean cast turned some serious events into non-serious ones
An SCD2 job forgot to close the previous version before opening the next
An inner join on a stale dimension silently dropped facts
A maintenance job detached a monthly partition and never re-attached it
Dedup ordered by ingestion time instead of change_seq, so an older version won
A fact row was loaded before its dimension row existed (late-arriving dimension)
A refactoring dropped a column that downstream reports still read (data reconciliation cannot see it)
A reporter's e-mail address was typed into the event description and copied into the warehouse
The latest job appended a redelivered event instead of collapsing it
A date parsed with day and month swapped landed outside the partition plan
A delete event was ignored, so a record entered in error is still reported
A developer added the subject's birth year to the analyst-facing subject dimension
A dimension reload inserted a subject twice with a new surrogate key
A mapping table shifted toxicity grades by one
